figures.finding: A child (under eighteen) may be employed to take part in artistic performances, notwithstanding the bars on work under thirteen and outside light work from thirteen to fifteen, only under a permit the Minister responsible for labour issues on a council's advice, which sets the hours and conditions; night work and nightclubs are barred to every child.

value.reachesWritingDirecting: no: the exception is for participating in artistic performances; other work is under ss. 33-34

figures.applies: Jamaica, Child Care and Protection Act ss. 2, 33-35, 39. The permit's usual conditions were not read (MLSS child labour unit pages hold none).

sources.said: "child" means a person under the age of eighteen years

employed for the purpose of participating in artistic performances. (2) A permit issued pursuant to subsection (1) shall specify the number of hours during which and the conditions under which the child may be so employed.
in night work or an industrial undertaking

figures.finding: A person is of full age at eighteen (Law Reform (Age of Majority) Act); a minor's contract is voidable; no statute read sets a child performer's earnings aside.

value.binding: voidable at the minor's option (common law)

figures.applies: Jamaica, as the National Land Agency's guidance states it.

sources.said: By virtue of the Law Reform (Age of Majority) Act a persons shall attain the age of majority and be of full age on attaining the age of eighteen (18) years.
